17   Klein to explain his vote.

18                SENATOR KLEIN:   Thank you, 

19   Mr. President.

20                I rise in support of this 

21   legislation.  But first, I'll just talk a little 

22   bit about the fight that was conducted over the 

23   summer on K2.  

24                This summer, unfortunately, can be 

25   dubbed -- not only downstate but also upstate, 


                                                                317

 1   and every place in between -- the summer of K2.  

 2   K2 is a synthetic drug known as Spice or Spike, 

 3   but it's nothing more than poison packaged with 

 4   clever names like Scooby Snacks, Bizarro and 

 5   Geeked Up.  You can get this poison for as little 

 6   as $5 at local grocery stores all over the State 

 7   of New York.

 8                During this fight I met a brave 

 9   mother, Deirdre Canaday, from Athens, New York, 

10   who lost her son, Aaron Stinson, to this poison.  

11   Deirdre transformed her pain into advocacy.  

12   She's truly someone I consider very, very brave.  

13                This tragedy with her son caused 

14   Deirdre to be a one-woman wrecking crew against 

15   the poison that we call K2.  She actually refers 

16   to it as "poison in a candy wrapper," and she is 

17   doing everything possible to make sure no other 

18   lives are taken.  

19                She's with us today.  Deirdre, can 

20   you please stand up?  I'd love everyone to 

21   welcome Deirdre to the chamber and give her a 

22   round of applause for protecting everyone.

23                (Standing ovation.)

24                SENATOR KLEIN:   Aaron, her son, was 

25   just 26 years old when he smoked Mr. Nice Guy 


                                                                318

 1   with his friends.  Unfortunately, Aaron never 

 2   woke up.  Who knows what was in the deceptive 

 3   baggy, a plant mixture sprayed with unlisted 

 4   chemicals.  K2 is marketed as legal weed, 

 5   incense, potpourri.  But the only thing we know, 

 6   that it's dangerous and lethal.  

 7                Like any 26-year-old, Aaron thought 

 8   he was having some fun because of these colorful 

 9   packages sold in delis and corner stores.  

10   Instead, his mother Deirdre is left to grieve.  

11   To tell his story, she's been traveling all over 

12   the state, appeared with myself in the Bronx at 

13   Jacobi Hospital, a hospital in my district, 

14   appeared in Syracuse with Senator David Valesky 

15   at an upstate summit.

16                In my district, over the summer 

17   alone, there were 700 visits within one month and 

18   statewide, over the summer, there was over 

19   6,800 people who were hospitalized from K2.  Most 

20   doctors, most law enforcement don't even know how 

21   to handle the situation.  They have ugly mood 

22   swings, become very violent, erratic, have 

23   epileptic seizures.  But we know one thing for 

24   sure, that's it preying on our young people.  

25                The legislation before you today is 


                                                                319

 1   a comprehensive package that was developed by 

 2   myself, Senator Valesky, and members of the 

 3   Republican Conference.  I think this package is 

 4   going to go a long way towards finally 

 5   criminalizing this drug and finally getting these 

 6   drugs off the street.  

 7                The piece of legislation that's 

 8   before you today is an "analog" bill.  This 

 9   analog law is something that I have passed in the 

10   State Senate for the last three years.  It's 

11   about time that the Assembly has taken up the 

12   bill.  It's very, very simple.  What it does is 

13   it allows New York to replicate the federal 

14   Analog Law.  

15                Right now when DEA actually finds 

16   that a drug that's being manufactured -- 

17   remember, most of these things are made in 

18   labs -- is mimicking the actual drug, we have the 

19   ability on the federal level to actually 

20   criminalize it or ban it.  By allowing the state 

21   to replicate or mimic the federal Analog Law, we 

22   can quickly ban all these substances.  

23                I know many of you in this chamber 

24   know that we banned bath salts.  Then they came 

25   to K2.  There was something that replicated LSD 


                                                                320

 1   last year called Bromo-Dragonfly.  We're not 

 2   going to be done once we actually ban or 

 3   criminalize the sale of K2.  

 4                So I think the way we get ahead of 

 5   the curve, the way we continue to criminalize 

 6   these dangerous substances, is by finally 

 7   adopting an analog law in New York State.  

 8                So again, I want to thank you, 

 9   Mr. President.  I urge all my colleagues to vote 

10   yes on this very important piece of legislation.

 8                SENATOR MONTGOMERY:   Yes, 

 9   Mr. President, to explain my vote.  

10                This bill, similarly to Senator 

11   Klein's bill, is an attempt to deal with the fact 

12   that this horrible drug is available so freely in 

13   this state.  And I certainly agree that we would 

14   love to ban it and to make it less possible for 

15   people, especially young people, to have access 

16   to it.

17                However, the bill includes, among 

18   the illegal entities, one who possesses or has 

19   control or abandons or transports.  And it also 

20   includes criminal sanctions beginning as high as 

21   a D felony.

22                So I think that we do not want at 

23   this point in time, though this is a very, very 

24   serious issue and the substance is an awful one, 

25   we do not want to go down the same road that we 


                                                                322

 1   already traveled with the war on drugs that we 

 2   have been through recently and that we are now 

 3   trying to correct.  And this is a slippery slope 

 4   in that direction.  

 5                So I'm going to vote no and I hope 

 6   that Senator Flanagan will make the necessary 

 7   amendments so that we can all support this 

 8   legislation.

 9                Thank you.  I vote no.

14                SENATOR FUNKE:   Thank you, 

15   Mr. President.  

16                I want to thank Senator Klein and 

17   Senator Valesky and the members of my own 

18   conference who have worked so hard on this 

19   particular issue.

20                As we work, ladies and gentlemen, to 

21   protect our children from the harmful effects of  

22   drugs, we have to work hard to stay ahead of the 

23   dealers and to stay ahead of the suppliers who 

24   design and manufacture these new drugs each and 

25   every day.  Therefore, when a new drug is 


                                                                324

 1   identified as something similar to a synthetic 

 2   drug that's already been banned, we have to act 

 3   on that, it seems to me, right away.  

 4                And this particular drug, alpha-PVP, 

 5   is also referred to as "flakka" or "gravel" on 

 6   the street.  And I'm sure many of you have read 

 7   the stories about it; it can be snorted, 

 8   injected, smoked or swallowed, and it has similar 

 9   effects to methamphetamine, in that it can lead 

10   to violent behavior.

11                And an example of that happened last 

12   year.  An 83-year-old Florida woman died of 

13   injuries sustained after she was brutally beaten 

14   by a man who was believed to be under the 

15   influence of flakka who attacked her inside her 

16   own home.

17                Last year the DEA arrested somebody 

18   in my region, in Livingston County, for 

19   possessing six pounds of this compound with the 

20   intent to sell.  And we have seen similar 

21   instances of it growing across the state and 

22   across the nation.

23                So by acting today, I think we are 

24   proactively and not reactively dealing with this 

25   problem in terms of how we seek to prevent our 


                                                                325

 1   kids from having access to these dangerous drugs.  

 2                So I want to thank everybody who 

 3   voted for this last year.  I vote aye, 

 4   Mr. President.  I urge my colleagues to do the 

 5   same.  Thanks.

24                SENATOR KLEIN:   Thank you, 

25   Mr. President.  


                                                                326

 1                This is the second piece of 

 2   legislation that I introduced in response to the 

 3   K2 epidemic.  This legislation amends the General 

 4   Business Law and I think provides I hope a 

 5   chilling effect to any businesses that are 

 6   thinking of selling K2.  

 7                First, it would provide a $2,000 

 8   fine for the first violation, a $5,000 fine for 

 9   the second violation, and finally a "three 

10   strikes you're out," where a third offense will 

11   result in the retailer's inability to sell 

12   cigarettes, alcohol, or lottery tickets.  And I 

13   think everyone knows that's the lifeblood of any 

14   convenience store, grocery store, or bodega.

15                This is something that's very, very 

16   important, because as we saw all over the state, 

17   especially in areas in downstate, according to 

18   the Governor's Executive Order there was only a 

19   $250 fine for actually selling K2 over the 

20   counter all over the state.  Needless to say, 

21   that was the cost of doing business and it didn't 

22   stop anyone from selling this nefarious 

23   substance.  

24                So I think the combination of the 

25   large fines and finally a "three strikes you're 


                                                                327

 1   out" will go a long way towards stopping the sale 

 2   of this substance in grocery stores.

 3                We also have a surrender program 

 4   that's created that if some businesses want to 

 5   come forward and surrender this substance, they 

 6   can.  

 7                So I think this is another 

 8   comprehensive approach which I hope will lead 

 9   towards the end of synthetic drugs.

10                Thank you, Mr. President.
